title: DesignBid
problem_statement: Seed and Series A startup product and engineering teams require high-quality product design for short 2-8 week sprints but cannot justify a full-time designer hire at $130-160K per year. Existing freelance platforms like Upwork surface 200+ unvetted candidates per post, consuming 10-15 hours of portfolio review and test coordination before work begins, while agencies charge $15-25K retainers that exceed pre-Series B budgets. This forces teams to either ship without design or accept work from generalist agencies that miss their product aesthetic. The gap is acute now because the post-2022 funding environment demands capital efficiency while design quality directly impacts user retention and fundraising narratives.
target_users: Seed-stage startup founder who is actively shipping product without a dedicated designer
Series A VP of Product managing a 3-6 person engineering team needing sprint-scoped design work
Contract product designer with 4+ years of SaaS or consumer app experience seeking vetted short-term engagements
Series A engineering lead who coordinates design handoffs and needs Figma-ready assets within sprint cycles
Seed-stage CTO who evaluates and approves contractor spend under $10K without board approval
user_stories: As a seed-stage startup founder who is actively shipping product without a dedicated designer, I want to browse pre-vetted designer profiles filtered by SaaS or consumer app vertical so that I can shortlist three candidates in under 30 minutes without reviewing unqualified portfolios

As a Series A VP of Product managing a 3-6 person engineering team needing sprint-scoped design work, I want to post a sprint brief with defined deliverables and a 2-8 week timeline so that I receive matched designer proposals within 24 hours and can start work within 3 business days

As a contract product designer with 4+ years of SaaS or consumer app experience seeking vetted short-term engagements, I want to complete a standardized async trial project during onboarding so that my skills are verified once and I avoid redundant test requests from every new client

As a Series A engineering lead who coordinates design handoffs and needs Figma-ready assets within sprint cycles, I want all project deliverables submitted through a structured handoff checklist inside the platform so that I receive annotated Figma files with component specs without back-and-forth clarification

As a seed-stage CTO who evaluates and approves contractor spend under $10K without board approval, I want transparent sprint-based pricing packages displayed before I contact a designer so that I can approve engagements independently and predict monthly design spend

As a Series A VP of Product managing a 3-6 person engineering team needing sprint-scoped design work, I want to view a designer's past sprint outcomes including client ratings and before-and-after screens so that I can assess aesthetic fit with our product before committing to a paid engagement

As a contract product designer with 4+ years of SaaS or consumer app experience seeking vetted short-term engagements, I want a dashboard showing upcoming sprint availability and client pipeline so that I can maintain a steady utilization rate of at least 80% without cold outreach
acceptance_criteria: A startup client can create a sprint brief, receive at least 3 matched designer proposals, and confirm an engagement in 3 calendar days or fewer from initial post

Designer profiles display vertical tags (e.g., SaaS, fintech, consumer mobile), years of experience, sprint availability calendar, and at least 5 rated past sprint outcomes before a client can contact them
All designers on the platform have completed a standardized async trial project scored by DesignBid reviewers on a published rubric before their profile is made visible to clients
Sprint-based pricing tiers ($2,500 / $5,000 / $8,000 per sprint) are displayed on each designer profile without requiring account creation or a sales call

The platform enforces a structured handoff milestone: designers must upload annotated Figma files with a completed component-spec checklist before the sprint is marked complete and payment is released
Clients can filter the designer marketplace by vertical, sprint duration, price tier, availability within 7 days, and tool stack (Figma, Framer, etc.) with results updating in under 2 seconds
A built-in async messaging thread is scoped per sprint engagement and retains all files, decisions, and feedback for 12 months post-sprint for both parties
Dispute resolution workflow routes unresolved handoff quality complaints to a DesignBid review team with a 48-hour SLA and escrow-held payment protection
Designer onboarding funnel accepts application, completes async trial, and returns an approval or rejection decision within 5 business days
Client time-to-hire is tracked per engagement and displayed in aggregate on an internal ops dashboard with a p50 and p90 breakdown

success_metrics.metric: Median client time-to-hire (sprint brief posted to engagement confirmed)
success_metrics.baseline: 21 days (current freelance platform average reported by target users)
success_metrics.target: 3 calendar days or fewer by end of Q2 post-launch

success_metrics.metric: Client portfolio-review hours eliminated per hire
success_metrics.baseline: 10-15 hours spent reviewing unvetted candidates on Upwork
success_metrics.target: Under 2 hours of active review time per hire within 6 months of launch

success_metrics.metric: Designer utilization rate (percentage of onboarded designers active on a paid sprint in any given month)
success_metrics.target: 70% average monthly utilization across active designer roster by month 6

success_metrics.metric: Gross Merchandise Volume (GMV) from completed sprint engagements
success_metrics.target: $500K cumulative GMV within 12 months of public launch

success_metrics.metric: Client repeat engagement rate (clients who book a second sprint within 90 days of completing their first)
success_metrics.target: 40% repeat engagement rate by end of month 9

success_metrics.metric: Designer acceptance rate through vetting funnel (applicants who pass async trial and are approved)
success_metrics.target: Calibrate to 25-35% acceptance rate to maintain quality signal; adjust rubric if rate exceeds 50% or falls below 15%

risks_open_questions: Supply-side cold start: How do we onboard enough pre-vetted designers across key verticals (SaaS, fintech, consumer) before launching to clients to avoid empty search results degrading trust on day one?
Pricing floor viability: Will $2,500 per sprint attract experienced designers with 4+ years of SaaS experience, or will price-sensitive clients depress designer quality expectations over time?

Async trial project bias: Does the standardized trial project format favor designers with strong UI execution but miss strategically strong designers who excel at problem framing and research synthesis?
Payment timing risk: If escrow is released only on handoff completion, how do we handle scope creep where clients delay approval to extract additional work without triggering a formal dispute?
Marketplace disintermediation: What contractual and UX mechanisms prevent clients and designers from moving off-platform after an initial introduction to avoid the platform fee on repeat engagements?
Vertical coverage gaps: The MVP must prioritize which verticals to vet designers against first — which 3-4 verticals represent the highest concentration of seed and Series A clients?

Designer churn from inconsistent sprint pipeline: If DesignBid cannot guarantee steady sprint volume, top designers may treat the platform as a secondary channel, reducing availability and response times

Legal classification risk: How does the platform ensure all engagements are structured to classify designers as independent contractors in compliance with state and federal labor laws across all U.S. jurisdictions?

Quality consistency at scale: As designer roster grows beyond 200, how does the ongoing quality audit process (re-scoring past work, monitoring client ratings) scale without a large internal ops team?
out_of_scope: Full-time or permanent designer placement or recruitment services
Design agency or multi-designer team engagements; platform is scoped to individual designer-to-startup matches only
User research, usability testing facilitation, or research ops services beyond visual and interaction design deliverables
Development or engineering services; platform does not match or vet front-end engineers or no-code builders
International designer or client onboarding in the MVP; launch is limited to U.S.-based designers and startups
Proprietary design tooling, whitelabeled Figma plugins, or in-platform prototyping or design creation tools
Enterprise or post-Series B company accounts with procurement workflows, MSAs, or volume licensing
Mobile app (iOS or Android) for the DesignBid platform in the initial release; web-only at launch
Automated AI-based portfolio scoring or generative design assistance features
Invoice factoring, designer income advances, or financial services beyond standard escrow-based sprint payments
